text: Methylation of histone H3 lysine-79 by Dot1p plays multiple roles in the UV damage response of Saccharomyces cerevisiae. A dot1 null mutation and a histone H3 lysine-79 point mutation both increased UV sensitivity, indicating lysine-79 methylation is required for efficient UV repair. Epistasis analysis of dot1 with UV repair genes revealed overlapping roles in nucleotide excision repair, post-replication repair, recombination repair, and RAD9-mediated checkpoint function. In contrast, epistasis analysis of the H3 lysine-79 point mutation showed the lysine-to-glutamic acid substitution affects only nucleotide excision repair and post-replication repair, suggesting this allele disrupts just a subset of lysine-79 methylation functions. The results indicate distinct, separable roles for histone H3 lysine-79 methylation in the UV damage response, potentially coordinating the various repair processes.
